correctness.rationale: The main formulas and rigidity check out, but the frozen Finding's unrestricted assertion that the uniform multiplier n-1 is larger is false at n=2 and n=3: K2=cot(pi/4)=1 and K3=csc(pi/6)=2. The sine ray itself is uniform in both cases. In each strict sorting chamber, conjugating the order permutation by first differences on the quotient by constants gives a weighted l1 matrix norm. Its normalized column j is the variation of a permuted suffix indicator divided by w_j. All j-element complements occur; summing the chamber bounds on a segment (continuity on ties) yields the global bound, and a small step in an open chamber attains it. At sine weights a j-cut has at most 2 min(j,n-j) edges; alternate across the consecutive central block and keep the labels constant outside, or use full alternation in the central even case. This realizes the largest weights, whose sum is K_n sin(pi j/n) by the finite sine progression. For arbitrary positive weights use the same cut rows A and a minimizing coordinate of w_i/s_i. The comparison Aw<=K_n w in the equality case propagates equality to the shared central column, and its full-support row then forces w proportional to s. This also proves strict improvement over uniform exactly for n>=4, where s_2/s_1=2 cos(pi/n)>1. Inspected CHECK.py and VERIFICATION.md without executing the script: the finite rational step/segment challenges and finite floating trigonometric checks are not the all-n proof. The defect does not change the sharp constants, but no repaired finding is submitted because of the exact prior coverage.
